name: Andrew "Flash" Tucker
caption: The reigning INWI World Heavyweight Champion, seeded into the CWC's own Chicago Championship tournament; won the eight-man tournament at the fed's first pay-per-view, pinning Sean Holloway, Outcast by Society and finally Jack Vars by submission (with Outcast by Society's outside interference) to become the first CWC Chicago Heavyweight Champion.

tenures.source: The fed's own newsletter (16 November 1998), naming the wrestler on its own Rankings list and/or its own Chicago/Cook County Championship tournament brackets; the fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998), for the match result below.
tenures.note: Beat Sean Holloway (first round), Outcast by Society (semifinal) and Jack Vars (final, figure-four leglock submission, with Outcast by Society clipping Vars' knee with a chair at ringside) to become the fed's first-ever Chicago Heavyweight Champion.

tenures.source: The promotion's own closing-weekend cards, 19-21 March 1999 (INWI Final PPV nights one to three)
The promotion's own second pay-per-view, 26 June 1999.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (andrew-flash-tucker-rspwf); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: "El Diablo" Eddie Deegan
caption: A first-round Chicago Championship tournament entrant, the reigning INWI Lightheavyweight Champion; beat The Pink Passion in the first round by roll-up before losing to Jack Vars in the semifinal.

tenures.source: The fed's own newsletter (16 November 1998), naming the wrestler on its own Rankings list and/or its own Chicago/Cook County Championship tournament brackets; the fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998), for the match result below.
tenures.note: Beat The Pink Passion by roll-up pinfall in the first round, then lost to Jack Vars in the semifinal (Northern Lights Suplex).

name: "The Extreme One" Tommy Grayson
caption: A first-round Cook County Championship tournament entrant from New York City; beat "Pitbull" Patrick Bergin and Dr. David Diversity before losing the title match to Duke Putrid in a ladder match.

tenures.source: The fed's own newsletter (16 November 1998), naming the wrestler on its own Rankings list and/or its own Chicago/Cook County Championship tournament brackets; the fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998), for the match result below.
tenures.note: Beat "Pitbull" Patrick Bergin (first round, roll-up) and Dr. David Diversity (semifinal, X-Treme Kick), then lost the Cook County Championship ladder match final to Duke Putrid.

identity.note: A common ring name reused across this hobby's fantasy rosters; registered separately from the existing RSPWF Top 200 poll stub of the same name, with no evidence connecting them.

name: "Ain't Nuttin' Personal" Antawn Carter
caption: A first-round Cook County Championship tournament entrant from Parkside, California; lost to Dr. David Diversity in a match disrupted by commentator Buck Martinez, then chokeslammed two of the Backstreet Boys during the fed's own concert interlude.

tenures.source: The fed's own newsletter (16 November 1998), naming the wrestler on its own Rankings list and/or its own Chicago/Cook County Championship tournament brackets; the fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998), for the match result below.
tenures.note: Lost to Dr. David Diversity in the first round after Buck Martinez's ringside interference turned the match into a brawl; later in the broadcast, chokeslammed both members of the Backstreet Boys before being pulled off by security.

name: "Absolute" Aaron Anderson
caption: A first-round Cook County Championship tournament entrant from Quebec, Canada, managed by Jacque Cartier; beat "Superstar" Tyrone Parker in the first round before losing to Duke Putrid in the semifinal.

tenures.source: The fed's own newsletter (16 November 1998), naming the wrestler on its own Rankings list and/or its own Chicago/Cook County Championship tournament brackets; the fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998), for the match result below.
tenures.note: Beat "Superstar" Tyrone Parker by roll-up in the first round, then lost to Duke Putrid's Devil's Tower Drop in the semifinal.

name: The Pink Passion
caption: A first-round Chicago Championship tournament entrant managed by his valet Rebekka; lost to "El Diablo" Eddie Deegan by roll-up after nearly forcing a submission with the Pink Dreams.

tenures.source: The fed's own newsletter (16 November 1998), naming the wrestler on its own Rankings list and/or its own Chicago/Cook County Championship tournament brackets; the fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998), for the match result below.
tenures.note: Lost to "El Diablo" Eddie Deegan in the first round: had the Pink Dreams submission hold locked in, but Deegan reached the ropes and rolled him up for the pin.

identity.note: A shared gimmick name; registered separately from the existing 'COW' wing's character of the same name, with no evidence connecting them.

name: "The Truth" Tony Shards
caption: A first-round Chicago Championship tournament entrant; the broadcast's own play-by-play shows him pinning an injured Jack Vars, but the fed's own subsequent newsletter and the tournament's own bracket both credit Vars with the win and advancement, and Shards was attacked and hospitalized in his locker room later in the broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own newsletter (16 November 1998), naming the wrestler on its own Rankings list and/or its own Chicago/Cook County Championship tournament brackets; the fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998), for the match result below.
tenures.note: The broadcast's own commentary shows Shards pinning Jack Vars for the three count after Vars was hurt on a botched piledriver, but the fed's own second newsletter and the tournament's later rounds (Vars facing Eddie Deegan in the semifinal) both credit Vars with the win -- a discrepancy in the fed's own record, not resolved here. Shards was later found unconscious and bleeding in his locker room by an unknown assailant, an angle this collection does not carry a resolution for.

name: Dr. David Diversity
caption: A first-round Cook County Championship tournament entrant from Boston, Massachusetts; beat Antawn Carter in a match disrupted by commentator Buck Martinez before losing to Tommy Grayson in the semifinal.

tenures.source: The fed's own newsletter (16 November 1998), naming the wrestler on its own Rankings list and/or its own Chicago/Cook County Championship tournament brackets; the fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998), for the match result below.
tenures.note: Beat Antawn Carter in the first round after Buck Martinez's ringside interference turned the match into a brawl, then lost to Tommy Grayson's X-Treme Kick in the semifinal.

name: Jack Vars
caption: A first-round Chicago Championship tournament entrant, managed by his valet Cindy McGlothlan; advanced through the tournament to the final, where he lost the Chicago Heavyweight Championship match to Andrew "Flash" Tucker by submission after Outcast by Society's outside interference.

tenures.source: The fed's own newsletter (16 November 1998), naming the wrestler on its own Rankings list and/or its own Chicago/Cook County Championship tournament brackets; the fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998), for the match result below.
tenures.note: Advanced past Tony Shards (first round, a finish the fed's own newsletter and bracket credit to him despite the broadcast's own play-by-play showing Shards land the pin) and "El Diablo" Eddie Deegan (semifinal, Northern Lights Suplex), then lost the Chicago Heavyweight Championship final to Andrew Tucker by submission (figure-four leglock) after Outcast by Society clipped his knee with a chair at ringside.

identity.note: A common ring name reused across this hobby's fantasy rosters; registered separately from the three existing characters of the same name, with no evidence connecting any of them.

name: "Superstar" Tyrone Parker
caption: A first-round Cook County Championship tournament entrant from Aspen, Colorado, eliminated by "Absolute" Aaron Anderson's roll-up.

tenures.source: The fed's own newsletter (16 November 1998), naming the wrestler on its own Rankings list and/or its own Chicago/Cook County Championship tournament brackets; the fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998), for the match result below.
tenures.note: Lost to "Absolute" Aaron Anderson by roll-up pinfall in the first round of the Cook County Championship tournament.

name: Randal Flagg
caption: A first-round entrant in the CWC's own Cook County Championship tournament; the newsletter's own text spells the name both 'Randal' and 'Randall' Flagg.

tenures.source: The fed's own newsletter (16 November 1998), naming the wrestler on its own Rankings list and/or its own Chicago/Cook County Championship tournament brackets.

name: "Superstar" Sean Holloway
caption: A first-round Chicago Championship tournament entrant from Lindale, Georgia, eliminated by Andrew "Flash" Tucker's Chronic Jumble Jaw superkick.

tenures.source: The fed's own newsletter (16 November 1998), naming the wrestler on its own Rankings list and/or its own Chicago/Cook County Championship tournament brackets; the fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998), for the match result below.
tenures.note: Lost to Andrew Tucker in the first round of the Chicago Championship tournament, kicked out of a Tornado DDT before Tucker connected twice with the Chronic Jumble Jaw for the pin.

name: Marcus Taylor
caption: A first-round Chicago Championship tournament entrant from Chicago, Illinois, eliminated by Outcast by Society's finisher, The Downfall.

tenures.source: The fed's own newsletter (16 November 1998), naming the wrestler on its own Rankings list and/or its own Chicago/Cook County Championship tournament brackets; the fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998), for the match result below.
tenures.note: Lost to Outcast by Society in the first round of the Chicago Championship tournament, pinned after The Downfall (an inverted corkscrew suplex into a 3/4 bulldog headlock).

name: "Pitbull" Patrick Bergin
caption: A first-round Cook County Championship tournament entrant from Washington, D.C., eliminated by Tommy Grayson's roll-up.

tenures.source: The fed's own newsletter (16 November 1998), naming the wrestler on its own Rankings list and/or its own Chicago/Cook County Championship tournament brackets; the fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998), for the match result below.
tenures.note: Lost to Tommy Grayson by roll-up pinfall in the first round of the Cook County Championship tournament, after a back-and-forth match that saw both men kick out of finishers.

name: Outcast by Society
caption: A first-round Chicago Championship tournament entrant from Providence, Rhode Island; beat Marcus Taylor before losing to Andrew "Flash" Tucker in the semifinal, then cost Jack Vars the title match by clipping his knee with a chair at ringside.

tenures.source: The fed's own newsletter (16 November 1998), naming the wrestler on its own Rankings list and/or its own Chicago/Cook County Championship tournament brackets; the fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998), for the match result below.
tenures.note: Beat Marcus Taylor with The Downfall in the first round, then lost to Andrew Tucker's Chronic Jumble Jaw in the semifinal. Later in the broadcast, interfered in the Chicago Heavyweight Championship final by clipping Jack Vars' knee with a steel chair, setting up Tucker's title-winning figure-four leglock.

name: Shawn Walsh
caption: Billed in the fed's own newsletter as the CWC's own in-story president, conducting the federation's contract talks.

tenures.source: The fed's own newsletter (16 November 1998), naming the wrestler on its own Rankings list and/or its own Chicago/Cook County Championship tournament brackets.
tenures.note: A role-alias persona: the newsletter's own byline credits its real out-of-character writer as the handler of a wrestler by this name, a detail redacted on the served page per the privacy rule; this character record carries only the ring/story name.

name: "Flatlander" Duke Putrid
caption: A three-hundred-fifty-pound cowboy from Devil's Tower, Wyoming, who won an eight-man tournament ladder match to become the CWC's first-ever Cook County Champion.

tenures.source: The fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998)
tenures.note: Beat Juan Garza, "Absolute" Aaron Anderson and Tommy Grayson across three rounds of the Cook County Championship tournament, retrieving the vacant title in a ladder match main event to become the fed's first Cook County Champion.

name: Juan Garza
caption: A first-round Cook County Championship tournament entrant from Bakersfield, California, eliminated by Duke Putrid's Devil's Tower Drop.

tenures.source: The fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998)

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (juan-garza-wopw-1999); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: Christian "Spotlight" Madison
caption: A newly signed CWC wrestler introduced by his ringside mouthpiece Carl Grant during the fed's pre-pay-per-view special, and billed there as a future Cook County title contender.

tenures.source: The fed's own pre-pay-per-view special, Countdown to Judgment Day (22 November 1998)
tenures.note: Introduced in a ringside interview segment on Countdown to Judgment Day; the fed's own second newsletter ranks him at 0-0 and schedules him against Brad "The Marksman" McNeil at the promotion's first weekly card, a match this collection does not carry a result for.

name: Brad "The Marksman" McNeil
caption: A CWC roster addition named in the fed's second newsletter, scheduled to face Christian Madison at the promotion's first weekly card.

tenures.source: The fed's own second newsletter, CWC Update Vol. I, #2 (28 November 1998)

name: Jade "The Blade" Steel
caption: A CWC roster addition named in the fed's second newsletter, scheduled to face Setzer Van Strife at the promotion's first weekly card.

caption: A CWC roster addition named in the fed's second newsletter, scheduled for a dark match at the promotion's first weekly card.

tenures.source: The fed's own second newsletter, CWC Update Vol. I, #2 (28 November 1998)

caption: A wrestler listed on the CWC's first roster in the fed's own player's guide under a bare ring name, absent from the roster two days later and never otherwise described.

caption: Jack Vars' own valet, walking him to the ring at the fed's first pay-per-view.

tenures.source: The fed's own pay-per-view broadcast, In Your Face: Judgment Day (26 November 1998)

name: Jim Houston
caption: The CWC's main play-by-play commentator, calling the promotion's broadcasts from its own studio and at ringside.

tenures.source: The fed's own Player's Guide, Version 1.0 (14 November 1998)
tenures.note: Named as the fed's own face color commentator in its player's guide, then called the fed's pre-pay-per-view special and its first pay-per-view broadcast in full alongside Buck Martinez.

name: Buck Martinez
caption: The CWC's heel color commentator, feuding on-air with his broadcast partner and repeatedly inserting himself physically into the promotion's own matches.

tenures.note: Named as the fed's own heel color commentator and a former EWC employee in the player's guide; at the fed's first pay-per-view he brawled ringside with Dr. David Diversity, Antawn Carter, a rival named "Tiny" Tim Thomas and the Backstreet Boys, and interfered directly in the Tucker-Holloway and Diversity-Grayson matches.

name: Joeboo
caption: The CWC's ring announcer, introducing every match at the fed's first pay-per-view.

tenures.source: The fed's own Player's Guide, Version 1.0 (14 November 1998)

name: Clubber Lang
caption: The CWC's head referee, officiating the promotion's tournament matches at its first pay-per-view.

tenures.source: The fed's own Player's Guide, Version 1.0 (14 November 1998)

name: Nick Diamond
caption: The CWC's main backstage correspondent, reporting live from the scene of an attack on Tony Shards during the fed's first pay-per-view.
